Name: Smith yourself
Author: namelessto
Description:
[center][size=5][b]Smith Yourself[/b][/size]
[i]Forge your upgrades yourself. No 2-day waits at Clint's, no timing your watering can around the rain.[/i][/center]

[size=4][b]Overview[/b][/size]

Adds a craftable anvil that lets you upgrade tools, weapons, boots, and open geodes yourself, plus a furnace that lets you strip an item back to its base form. After joining the Adventurer's Guild, Marlon will mail you an anvil, or you can buy one (and a furnace) from the Guild Shop. Marlon also sends a pair of old boots when you get the rusty sword, to help you get started.

[size=4][b]Features[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Upgrade tools, weapons, and boots using a timing-based mini-game.[/*]
[*]Two mini-game scoring modes: aim for a moving Sweet Spot, or the original Legacy hold-at-the-top method.[/*]
[*]A Perfect hit can grant tools and weapons a random bonus enchantment, and each enchantment can be turned on or off per tool type.[/*]
[*]Strip an item back to its base form at the furnace if you'd rather start over.[/*]
[*]Break open geodes and mystery boxes at your own anvil.[/*]
[*]Your skill level reduces difficulty and can save materials on a high score.[/*]
[*]Supports axes, pickaxes, hoes, watering cans, fishing rods, scythes, pans, trash cans, backpacks, and trinkets.[/*]
[*]Custom weapons and boots with full upgrade paths available from the Guild Shop.[/*]
[*]Four mini-game difficulty settings: Normal, Simple, Hard, and Skip.[/*]
[*]Fully configurable through Generic Mod Config Menu.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]How to Use[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Equip the item you want to upgrade.[/*]
[*]Make sure you have the required materials in your inventory.[/*]
[*]Interact with the anvil and play the mini-game to build your score.[/*]
[*]A Critical score saves 25% of the required materials. A Perfect score does the same for tools/weapons but also grants a bonus enchantment (or, on items that can't be enchanted, a bigger discount instead). Failure costs 25% but does not upgrade the item.[/*]
[*]Hold [b]nothing[/b] and interact with the anvil to open a manual showing all upgrade costs based on your current config.[/*]
[/list]
To open geodes: hold a geode or mystery box and interact with the anvil.

[youtube]QHaiVtnkIkI[/youtube]

[size=4][b]Mini-game Difficulty & Scoring[/b][/size]

[spoiler]
[b]Mini-game Difficulty[/b]

[list]
[*][b]Normal[/b]: standard number of hits per tier.[/*]
[*][b]Simple[/b]: single hit only.[/*]
[*][b]Hard[/b]: 2 extra hits per tier; the bar speeds up after each hit (speed increment is configurable).[/*]
[*][b]Skip[/b]: upgrade instantly without the mini-game.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Scoring Method[/b]

[list]
[*][b]Sweet Spot[/b] [i](default)[/i]: a target zone moves along the bar each swing. Land inside it for a Critical, dead-center for a Perfect.[/*]
[*][b]Legacy[/b]: the original method. Hold your swing for the top of the bar.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[size=4][b]Perfect Enchantments[/b][/size]

[spoiler]
Landing a Perfect hit on a tool or weapon has a chance to grant it a random enchantment, on top of the usual Critical-tier material discount. This is on by default and can be turned off in the config, and each enchantment can be toggled per tool type from its own config page.

Boots, Backpacks, Trash Cans, Scythes, and Trinkets can't carry enchantments, so a Perfect on those gives a bigger material discount instead (30% by default, configurable). Going for Perfect is never a worse bet than settling for a Critical, no matter what you're upgrading.[/spoiler]

[size=4][b]Furnace[/b][/size]

[spoiler]
Available at the Guild Shop for 700g. Hold the tool, weapon, or pair of boots you want to reset and interact with the furnace to strip it back to its base form. There's no minigame and no refund. Backpacks, Trash Cans, and Trinkets can't be downgraded this way. Hold nothing and interact with it for a manual.[/spoiler]

[size=4][b]Upgrade Paths[/b][/size]

[spoiler]
Basic tools follow the same material tiers as vanilla, but all costs can be changed in the config.

[b]Fishing Rods[/b]
[list]
[*]Bamboo Pole → Training Rod → Fiberglass Rod → Iridium Rod → Advanced Iridium Rod[/*]
[*]The Training Rod upgrade is skipped by default and can be re-enabled in the config.[/*]
[*]Requirements:
[list]
[*]Bamboo → Training: 100 wood[/*]
[*]Training → Fiberglass: 10 refined quartz[/*]
[*]Fiberglass → Iridium: 5 iridium bars[/*]
[*]Iridium → Advanced: 40 iridium bars[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
[b]Scythes[/b]
[list]
[*]Scythe → Golden Scythe: 25 gold bars[/*]
[*]Golden Scythe → Iridium Scythe: 40 iridium bars[/*]
[/list]
[b]Trash Cans[/b]
[list]
[*]Each tier costs the standard material (e.g. 5 copper bars). Hold a trash item when interacting.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Backpacks[/b]
[list]
[*]12 Slots → 24 Slots: 50 fiber[/*]
[*]24 Slots → 36 Slots: 3 cloth[/*]
[/list]
[b]Trinkets[/b]
[list]
[*]Each upgrade costs 3 iridium bars (configurable).[/*]
[*]Upgrades can jump levels randomly; stats only ever improve, staying within vanilla limits.[/*]
[*]Magic Quiver paths:
[list]
[*]Regular → Rapid / Heavy / Perfect[/*]
[*]Rapid → Rapid / Perfect[/*]
[*]Heavy → Heavy / Perfect[/*]
[*]Perfect cannot be upgraded further.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
[b]Weapons[/b]
[list]
[*]Three rusty starter weapons (sword, mace, and dagger) can be bought from the Guild Shop and upgraded.[/*]
[*]Each tier costs the same as standard tools (5x copper bars → 5x iron bars, etc.).[/*]
[*]The final tier requires 20x iridium bars and 20x star shards for swords and maces, or 10x star shards for the dagger.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Boots[/b]
[list]
[*]Starter boots can be upgraded through five tiers, ending with the new [b]Nebula Striders[/b]: Weathered → Copper-Plated → Steel-Plated → Gilded → Iridium Vanguard → Nebula Striders.[/*]
[*]Each tier costs the same as standard tools (5x copper bars → 5x iron bars, etc.), except the final tier, which requires 20x iridium bars and 20x star shards.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[size=4][b]Skill Requirements[/b][/size]

[spoiler]
Your relevant skill level reduces mini-game difficulty and can lower material costs on high scores.
[list]
[*]Axe → Foraging[/*]
[*]Pickaxe & Pan → Mining[/*]
[*]Hoe, Watering Can & Scythe → Farming[/*]
[*]Fishing Rod → Fishing[/*]
[*]Trash Can & Backpack → Overall Farmer Level[/*]
[*]Weapons, Boots & Trinkets → Combat[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[size=4][b]Configuration[/b][/size]

All options are in [b]config.json[/b] or through [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] in-game.

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] 4.2.1 or later[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] [i](optional, for in-game config)[/i][/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url].[/*]
[*]Download and unzip into your [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/Mods[/font] folder.[/*]
[*]Run the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]

Works on an existing save. The anvil and furnace are available right after you join the Adventurer's Guild, either through Marlon's mail or the Guild Shop.
